descriptors.concept_name: Payment Of Debts By Contributory And Extent Of Set-Off [Section 295]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may direct any contributory listed during winding up to pay due amounts, excluding regular calls. In unlimited or limited structures under specific conditions, offsets against independent transactions may be permitted.
inclusion: money due from a contributory other than regular calls
set-offs on independent contracts for unlimited companies or eligible directors
set-offs against subsequent calls after full creditor settlement
exclusion: dividends or profits due to a member
call money required under the Act prior to full creditor clearance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular share calls under Section 296 which are levied specifically to satisfy debts and liquidation expenses.

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal possesses the authority to balance and reconcile mutual rights among contributories during liquidation. Any resulting surplus assets are subsequently distributed to the rightful beneficiaries.
inclusion: balancing claims and liabilities among contributories
distribution of company surplus to entitled persons
exclusion: satisfaction of external creditor claims prior to adjustment
determination of preferential payments under separate sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from the power to make calls under Section 296, focusing instead on internal equity and surplus allocation among shareholders.

descriptors.definition: When corporate assets are inadequate to cover total liabilities, the Tribunal can direct the payment of liquidation expenses out of available funds. Such costs are settled based on an inter se priority determined by the Tribunal.
inclusion: payment of winding up costs, charges, and expenses from insufficient assets
fixing inter se priorities for expense settlement
exclusion: ordinary operational debts outside liquidation expenses
unauthorized disbursements not sanctioned by the Tribunal
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general debt settlement rules as it specifically prioritizes administrative winding up costs when assets fall short.

descriptors.concept_name: Power To Summon Persons Suspected Of Having Property Of Company, Etc. [Section 299]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal can summon officers, suspected possessors of company property, or knowledgeable individuals after appointing a provisional liquidator or ordering a winding up. It can examine them on oath, require book production, and order the delivery of assets or payment of debts.
inclusion: summoning officers or third parties suspected of holding company property or books
examining summoned persons via word of mouth, interrogatories, or affidavits
ordering indebted persons to pay or property holders to deliver assets to the liquidator
exclusion: prejudicing lawful liens claimed over produced books and papers during determination
proceedings conducted prior to provisional liquidator appointment or winding up order
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 300 by focusing broadly on gathering information, recovering hidden assets, and securing books from any suspected persons rather than targeted fraud investigations of promoters.

descriptors.concept_name: Power To Order Examination Of Promoters, Directors, Etc. [Section 300]
descriptors.definition: Upon receiving a liquidator report alleging fraud in formation or business conduct, the Tribunal can direct implicated persons to attend and undergo examination on oath. Such individuals are entitled to legal representation and can apply for exculpation from charges.
inclusion: directing officers or promoters named in a fraud report to be examined
permitting professional assistance such as chartered accountants or legal practitioners for the examined person
liquidator participation and duty to respond to exculpation applications
exclusion: general inquiries into company affairs lacking a formal liquidator fraud report
unrepresented testimonies without access to the foundational report
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Section 299 general summons because it specifically activates upon a liquidator's fraud report regarding promotion, formation, or business conduct.

descriptors.concept_name: Arrest Of Person Trying To Leave India Or Abscond [Section 301]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may order the detention of a contributory or person holding company assets and seize their movable property if there is an attempt to abscond or conceal assets. This action prevents the evasion of calls or avoidance of company affairs examinations.
inclusion: detaining contributories or asset holders about to leave India or abscond
seizing books, papers, and movable property to prevent concealment
exclusion: detention for ordinary civil debts outside winding up contexts
seizure of immovable property under this specific detention provision
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from standard asset recovery proceedings as it provides an emergency preventive arrest and seizure mechanism against flight risk individuals.

descriptors.definition: When company affairs are completely wound up or when deemed just and reasonable, the Tribunal orders company dissolution upon a liquidator application. A copy of the order is forwarded to the Registrar for recording a minute of dissolution.
inclusion: dissolution orders following complete winding up or when just and reasonable
forwarding dissolution orders to the Registrar within thirty days
recording minutes of dissolution in the company register
exclusion: ongoing liquidation proceedings where assets or liabilities remain unaddressed
voluntary winding up procedures managed under alternative frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Differs from operational winding up steps as it marks the final legal termination of the corporate entity's existence.

descriptors.concept_name: Appeals From Orders Made Before Commencement Of Act [Section 303]
descriptors.definition: Orders made in winding up proceedings immediately prior to the commencement of the current Act remain unaffected by new provisions. Appeals against such legacy orders must be pursued before the competent authority designated prior to commencement.
inclusion: preserving the enforcement and operation of pre-existing court winding up orders
filing appeals before authorities competent prior to the new enactment
exclusion: winding up orders initiated and processed under the provisions of the current Act
maintainable appeals by disqualified stakeholders as per judicial precedent
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from modern winding up rules by protecting historical transitional orders and their legacy appellate pathways.

descriptors.concept_name: Debts Of All Descriptions To Be Admitted To Proof [Section 324]
descriptors.definition: All claims and contingent, future, or uncertain debts against a company are admissible to proof during winding up. A fair estimation of the value is determined for claims that are uncertain, contingent, or sound only in damages.
inclusion: admitting all present, future, certain, or contingent debts
claims sounding only in damages
making a just estimate of uncertain claim values
exclusion: debts barred by insolvency rules applicable to insolvent companies where inconsistent
unsupported claims lacking ascertainable estimation parameters
nearby_distinctions: Differs from preferential payments by providing a broad gateway for all creditor claims to enter the proof stage, regardless of their contingent nature.

descriptors.definition: During winding up, workmen's dues and specific portions of secured creditors' un-realized debts rank above all other claims. These priority sums must be paid in full within a strict timeline from asset sales before general secured debt disbursements.
inclusion: prioritizing workmen's dues pari passu with eligible secured creditor shortfalls
settling specified pre-winding up wages and salary obligations within thirty days of asset sale
proportional abatement when assets are insufficient
exclusion: standard unsecured debts lacking statutory priority status
payments made to secured creditors prior to settling mandatory workmen portions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard preferential payments under Section 327 by overriding even secured creditors' charges up to the statutory workmen's portion.

descriptors.definition: Subject to overriding provisions, specific government revenues, employee wages, holiday remuneration, statutory contributions, and welfare fund dues within designated pre-winding up timeframes are paid in priority. These claims represent statutory preference categories during asset distribution.
inclusion: government taxes, cesses, and rates due within twelve months of the relevant date
employee wages, salary, and holiday remuneration within statutory limits
contributions under insurance, compensation, and employee welfare funds
exclusion: debts falling outside the specified preceding time windows
ordinary unsecured commercial claims not designated as preferential
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from Section 326 overriding payments because preferential taxes and standard employee dues rank behind workmen overriding charges and secured creditor parity.

descriptors.definition: Transactions favoring specific creditors or sureties executed within six months prior to a winding up application that place them in a better liquidation position can be declared invalid by the Tribunal. The Tribunal may order restoration of the original position.
inclusion: property transfers, deliveries, payments, or executions favoring creditors or sureties within six months
Tribunal orders declaring preferential transactions invalid and restoring positions
exclusion: transactions occurring outside the six-month statutory window prior to application
transfers made in good faith and for valuable consideration under ordinary business terms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Section 329 transfers not in good faith, focusing specifically on preferential treatment of existing creditors or sureties within a six-month window rather than general one-year non-ordinary transfers.
